subject: Discovery recap: embeddings & reranking for BrightCart

Subject: Discovery recap: embeddings & reranking for BrightCart

Hi Ethan / Sarah —

Thanks again for taking time today — great first conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we all have the same expectations. Let me know if I missed anything.

Attendees (on call): Ethan Moore (BrightCart), Sarah Li (BrightCart), Marissa Cole (Redwood), Vivek Kulkarni (Redwood), Rishi Malhotra (Redwood)

Pain points / goals
- Relevance drop for long-tail queries and seasonal catalogs — manual tuning of ranking rules has been brittle.
- Reranking step is a bottleneck: current p95 latency ~250-300ms under peak, aiming to get p95 < 120ms (ideally <100ms) for user-facing reranks.
- Index scale: ~50M product embeddings (current dim 1536), nightly batch ingests plus near-real-time updates (hundreds/s).
- Cost sensitivity: want to keep inference unit costs predictable; initial pilot budget constrained.

Current stack (from call)
- Embeddings generated offline (existing model) and stored in Milvus for vector search; Postgres for product metadata; Redis for session caches.
- Frontend runs a candidate retrieval (approx NN) -> rerank pipeline that calls a model-based scorer.

Success criteria for pilot
- Demonstrate quality uplift vs current rules on held-out query set (target: +5-8% NDCG).
- Latency: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 120ms for reranking endpoint under expected pilot qps.
- Ops: ability to push nightly full-index refreshes and handle 1k qps peak with graceful degradation.

Technical notes discussed
- Vector DB: Milvus today; open to alternatives or a hybrid approach (Milvus + Redis/flash cache) for hot segments.
- Indexing: HNSW for ANN with sharding by product domain looks best for your shape/traffic.
- Caching: session-level prefix caching and per-user top-k caching will reduce redundant model calls.

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood SE deep-dive (technical) — Rishi to scope required dataset samples and run sizing estimates (we suggested a 60-90 minute tech session).
2) Pilot plan & mutual action plan (attached) — outline milestones for ingest, evals, perf tests.
3) Provide a small sample export (10k-50k vectors + metadata) and a representative query set for offline evals.
4) Redwood to provide a ballpark sizing & cost estimate for 50M vectors at expected peak (Rishi will follow up).

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.pdf, embedding-scale.csv (high-level index stats we captured during call)

If that looks right, I'll put the tech-deep-dive on the calendar for next week.

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: embeddings & reranking for BrightCart — follow-up items

Ethan / Sarah —

Thanks — I'll scope the tech session. A few quick notes ahead of the call so we can optimize the agenda: 

1) Index sizing & performance (ballpark numbers to set expectations)
- 50M vectors @ 1536 dims (float32) ~ 300-350GB raw; with 8-bit quantization / product-specific sharding we expect on-disk RAM/flash needs to be ~60-120GB depending on index parameters.
- For HNSW with 32 shards (example), we expect single-query p95 ~30-80ms depending on hardware class and whether rescoring runs locally vs remote.

2) Model & quantization recommendations
- Use a smaller embedder (768-1536 dims) if it preserves quality — reduces index size/cost.
- Consider int8 or product-aware PQ for dense storage; Redwood Optimize can recommend config tuned to your query distribution.

3) Rerank architecture options
- Option A: Candidate retrieval from Milvus -> in-memory proxy (Redis/flash) -> on-GPU reranker for final scoring. Good p95 but higher infra cost.
- Option B: Two-stage lightweight rerank (cheap model on CPU for pruning + smaller GPU-only final scorer). Lower cost, slightly higher tail latency.

4) Cache & batching patterns
- Nightly full rebuilds + incremental micro-batches for updates (we recommend using sequence numbers to apply deltas).
- Continuous batching at the proxy layer to amortize model overhead; Redwood can provide automatic batching configs during pilot.

For the cost ballpark: if you run a dedicated cluster sized for 1k qps peak (mixed CPU+GPU with hot caching), expect pilot infra from low-dollars-per-hour to mid-hundreds-per-hour depending on committed capacity and instance choices. We'll provide a more specific estimate after we see the sample and confirm expected P95 targets.

Attachments: redwood_technical_estimate.xlsx (contains example shard configs and perf sims)

—Rishi
